hero.name: Sanghyeon Shin
hero.lead: A frontend developer who builds the screens people actually use, then keeps running and fixing them after launch.
hero.summary:
Over two years I've built and shipped 15+ services with React, Next.js, and TypeScript. As a LIKELION intern running a 2,000-person national hackathon, **I built a finals tournament console (Next.js · Supabase), a script that checked 562 submitted repos, and an FAQ Discord bot, and put them to work on site**; a judge's vote reached the stage screen in a measured 2.2 seconds.

Building tools for a live event taught me to **close off the failures you can't undo before adding features**. I re-validate requests on the server, keep state consistent when several people operate at once, and build a way forward for when the network drops. Next, I want to be **a developer who keeps improving the product from the logs and data users leave behind**.

principles.heading: How I work.
principles.to_projects: See how the three principles played out in code in the projects

items.t:
I keep requirements in one document
and build to it.
items.d: Requirements and the reasons behind decisions go into a single dated SPEC document, and code and tests are written against it. Because I can check the intent myself while building, planning and development stop drifting apart.

items.t:
I close off the failures
you can't undo first.
items.d: Permissions and state transitions are re-validated on the server instead of trusting the client. Concurrent edits, late requests, and network failures, the things you can't recover from on site, get handled before new features.

items.t:
After launch, I read the logs
and fix it again.
items.d: Launch is where user data starts coming in. Just as the FAQ bot's daily report of unanswered questions fed its knowledge base, I bring what real use turns up into the next release.

figures.heading: What the tools I built changed
figures.sub: Only what actually changed once the tools I built went into operation.

changes.label: Participant inquiries
changes.d: A Discord bot over the 78-item FAQ answered with keyword matching first and an LLM fallback, so 80.8% of inquiries got an instant answer at zero API cost. The staff spent 15 minutes a day on the unanswered-question report, filling gaps.
changes.basis: Basis: one month after the FAQ bot · 229 questions · 0 unanswered · staff time includes log review and answer updates · 14th hackathon

changes.label: Submission checks
changes.d: A Python script found post-deadline commits on every branch of every repo, and snapshot-JSON comparison caught force-pushes, deleted branches, and public-to-private flips. The tool only produced evidence; the staff ruled by criteria agreed before the scan.
changes.basis: Basis: after the 314-team deadline · 5 violations found · 14th hackathon

changes.label: Finals results reveal
changes.d: The server checked each vote's judge code, allowlist, and match state before saving it, and the stage screen read the state every 1.5 seconds: 2.2 seconds from vote to screen.

changes.label: 13th cohort session attendance
changes.d: Members scan the QR code on the staff screen with their phones and the check-in is recorded on the server right away; scans more than 20 minutes after the session starts are marked late automatically, so the roll shows only late and absent members.
changes.basis: Basis: 45 members of HUFS LIKELION's 13th cohort · WelcomeKit PWA
